svg.text: When to use the compile-time perfect hash — and which mode you get
numbers: Apple M3 Max, shuffled hits, ns per lookup · francisco/experimental, 2026-08-31
Is the key set known when you write the code?
(protocol verbs, header names, struct fields, a symbol universe)
no
runtime table
absl::flat_hash_map; ≤8-byte symbols: pack into u64 first
(2.4–3.0 ns on tickers, 6–8 ns on strings)
yes
Are all keys a single byte?
yes
make_perfect_set: direct 256-entry table
0.5 ns — a plain if/switch on the byte ties it (0.4 ns)
no
How many keys?
classic shapes
classic mode: N ≤ 255 with keys ≥ 8 B, or tiny sets (N < 8)
hash = len + asso[pos₁][k[pos₁]] (+ …), 1–2 chosen bytes, 4 instructions
tiers picked automatically: gperf → hash-and-displace → seeded whole-key
1.27–2.05 ns; 0.00 branch misses on every set incl. Counters
N ≥ ~50: set -fconstexpr-steps (clang default ≈ 1 M steps)
wide shapes
wide mode: N > 255, or short keys (≤ 7 B) with N ≥ 8
whole-key multiply → bucket → u16 pilot → slot; verified at compile time
S&P 100 1.32 · S&P 500 1.27 · all 5 581 Nasdaq symbols 1.73 (36–40 instr)
generated lists: make_wide_perfect_index_map<array>() — 5 s compile @ 5 581
beyond 65 535 keys or 4 080-byte keys: pthash / absl at run time
How long is the longest key? (verification strategy, chosen by MaxKeyLen)
≤ 4 B → two overlapping halfword loads + length, one 64-bit compare
≤ 8 B → page-safe 16-B load, tbl mask, one 64-bit compare (tickers: 1.8 ns @100)
≤ 16 B → tbl mask + cmeq, one vector compare (HTTP headers: 1.3 ns)
17–32 B → 2 chunks, branch-free for any address (Headers50 1.89, Counters 1.85)
> 32 B → ⌈L/16⌉ chunks, sliding masks, one guard (Java FQCNs 54 B: 2.05 ns; was 23 ns)
How long is the longest key? (wide mode)
≤ 7 B → one 64-bit lane, length in the top byte; compare = eor + tst
value ≤ 16 bit fits in the spare bytes → fused, no value table
≤ 15 B → two lanes (ldp), length in lane 1's top byte
16 B … 4 080 B → hash over all lanes, ⌈L/16⌉-chunk compare + length
every byte of the key feeds the hash: no position search, no 16-position wall
What the numbers assume — and where every table looks the same
• Hits or misses only: 0.00–0.01 branch misses per lookup, ~5–7 cycles. Misses are slightly faster than hits (the compare rejects; nothing else is fetched).
• Random 50/50 hit/miss streams: every structure pays the caller's `if (found)` mispredict (~15 cycles). Ours: 7.7 ns @ S&P 500 vs 8–12 ns for the field.
• Working set: keep the table in L1 (128 KB here). Nasdaq's 64 KB key table + input stream costs ~2 cycles over S&P 500 at the same instruction count.
Do not reach for it when…
• keys arrive at run time (config files, user input) — there is nothing to solve at compile time;
• the set changes between builds faster than you can rebuild — compile time is 0.1 s (10 keys) … 5 s (5 581 keys) per translation unit that instantiates it;
• you need more than 65 535 keys, keys longer than 4 080 bytes, embedded NUL bytes at the end of keys, or a table that must be identical across big/little-endian targets.
